The drawing shows a benzaldehyde ring with two substituents, joined through sulfur to a tolyl ring.

**Right ring (benzaldehyde).** The CHO group sits at the top carbon. The carbon to its left carries S, so S is ortho to the aldehyde. The carbon at lower right carries NO2. Numbering from the CHO carbon as C1: C2 (S) is the upper-left carbon, then C3 (lower left), C4 (bottom), C5 (lower right, NO2), and C6 (upper right). NO2 is therefore para to the S carbon, which makes this 2-(arylthio)-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.

**Left ring (tolyl).** The ring is attached to S at its upper-right carbon, and a methyl group sits at the far left, para to S. This is a p-tolyl group.

**SMILES.** O=Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Sc1ccc(C)cc1

Check on the right ring: c1 (CHO), then c (C6), c(NO2) (C5), c (C4), c (C3), c1 (C2, bearing S). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Sc1ccc(C)cc1
